mara.name: Mara the Mason
mara.summary: Laid half the current walls and still complains about green timber.
mara.wants: Straight courses and dry stone that will outlast her.
mara.needs: To believe the walls she lays will still stand when she is gone.

dialogue.default: The courses are true enough. For now.
dialogue.afterGreenTimber: That wood will twist before winter. I told you.
dialogue.afterGrowth: New hands. Give them a trowel that fits.
dialogue.afterMission: You brought the road home in your boots. Scrape them before you track the hall.
dialogue.afterLevel: New rows mean new courses. Do not rush the green timber.

old-bell.name: Old Bell
old-bell.summary: Counts the flocks by bell, not by dog, and keeps the bent-clapper story alive.
old-bell.wants: Every sheep accounted for at grey dawn.
old-bell.needs: Someone younger to learn the three-clack warning before the owls go silent.

dialogue.default: Three clacks means the owls have gone quiet. Listen.
dialogue.afterRaid: Three clacks and the owls went quiet. You heard it too.
dialogue.afterGrowth: New hands. Teach them the bells before the next dark.
dialogue.afterPastureThreat: Count the bells twice. Something walked the fence.
dialogue.afterMission: I rang you out and I rang you in. The clapper remembers both.
dialogue.afterLevel: Another feast-length of ringing. The rope will hold.

issa.name: Second-Lantern Issa
issa.summary: Keeps Sella's old seed stories and the Chart Log.
issa.wants: Every useful plant and every useful chart written down before it is forgotten.
issa.needs: Proof that the Long Dusk is still a place where things can be saved, not only endured.

dialogue.default: The charts remember what the living forget. Write it down.
dialogue.afterMissionReturn: A new page for the Chart Log. The road gave us something worth keeping.
dialogue.afterFailedHearth: Mark the dry well. No one rebuilds on a lie.
dialogue.afterGrowth: Beds before bodies. The log is clear on that.
dialogue.afterMission: I inked the expedition. The blank page is smaller now.
dialogue.afterLevel: The chart gains a row. Beds before bodies still holds.

tomm.name: Tomm Waterwise
tomm.summary: Says water is older than walls and will not say it twice.
tomm.wants: Ponds that breathe and pastures that rest when they must.
tomm.needs: A village that does not overdraw the land until it goes pale.

dialogue.default: Water is older than walls. Build it first.
dialogue.afterDarkPond: Rest it. Overdrawn land goes pale.
dialogue.afterGrowth: More mouths. Watch the pond at night.
dialogue.afterMission: The water did not leave while you were gone. Good.
dialogue.afterLevel: More mouths. Rest the pond a night if it goes dark.

sarella.name: Sarella of the Forge
sarella.summary: Honest steel, charcoal arithmetic; will not choose who goes short when coal runs thin.
sarella.wants: Edges that stay true and coal that arrives on time.
sarella.needs: A roster that can afford the master's standard without lying about the steel.

dialogue.default: Pick the work, not the shine.
dialogue.afterScarcity: Coal is thin. I will not choose who goes short — you will.
dialogue.afterGrowth: New hands want steel. Bring them when the coal holds.
dialogue.afterMission: Edges came back true. Pay the coal when the wagons can.
dialogue.afterLevel: More hands want steel. I will not choose who goes short.

mooncleric.name: The Mooncleric
mooncleric.summary: Light steadies; it does not smite. Answers the double-tap with bread, not chain.
mooncleric.wants: Ransom over slaughter when the watchfire is tapped twice.
mooncleric.needs: A Manner that still believes steadiness is enough theology.

dialogue.default: Light steadies. It does not smite.
dialogue.afterRaid: You held. The lamps still burn.
dialogue.afterRansom: Bread, not chain. The warning held.
dialogue.afterGrowth: More lamps in the bowl. I will not call it salvation.
dialogue.afterLevel: More lamps in the bowl. I will not call it salvation.

wayfinder.name: The Wayfinder
wayfinder.summary: Marks failed hearths on the Timber Line so no one rebuilds on a dry well.
wayfinder.wants: Honest chalk: every dry well, every dead oven, every road that still feeds.
wayfinder.needs: A village that builds water before walls when the map says so.

dialogue.default: Build water first. Then the wall.
dialogue.afterRaid: The chart is honest about what you walked.
dialogue.afterFailedHearth: Mark it. No one rebuilds on a lie.
dialogue.afterGrowth: New land on the chalk. Mark the dry wells first.
dialogue.afterMission: The Timber Line chart is honest about what you walked.
dialogue.afterLevel: New land on the chalk. Mark the dry wells first.

armorer.name: The Armorer
armorer.summary: Plates first, pride later; works dents that held back into soft leather.
armorer.wants: Racks filled with hide and plate, not hopes.
armorer.needs: Shoulders measured before the next horn.

dialogue.afterRaid: Count the dents. The ones that held can be worked again.
dialogue.afterScarcity: I can plate four more. After that the roster gets thin.
dialogue.afterGrowth: New shoulders to fit. Bring them before the next horn.
dialogue.afterMission: Plate came home dented, not broken. Good.
dialogue.afterLevel: Racks need filling. Hide and plate, not hopes.

rue.name: Rue the turncloak
rue.summary: Walked out of the treeline with empty hands and a full ledger; ran with the pale bands three winters and now chalks them by name on the hall door.
rue.wants: One clean defense to prove the price was worth paying.
rue.needs: To believe the walls she once scoped will hold against the bands she once ran with.

dialogue.default: They stack their torches low and come at the east joints. Ask me how I know.
dialogue.afterRaid: Not one stone out of place. That is the only ledger I keep now.
dialogue.afterScarcity: Fire is cheap. Regret is dear. Spend the pitch, not the men.
dialogue.afterGrowth: New hands. Teach them the trap-lines before the next horn.
dialogue.afterMission: They stacked torches where I said. You listened.
dialogue.afterLevel: Bigger walls make louder targets. Stay sharp.

master-tam.name: Master Tam
master-tam.summary: Head of the school, keeper of the primer; teaches letters first, ledgers second, and loyalty always.
master-tam.wants: Three filled stools and a roll worth chalking.
master-tam.needs: Graduates who carry the trade further than he can walk it himself.

dialogue.default: Letters first, ledgers second, loyalty always. Sit.
dialogue.afterRaid: The school stood. Lessons resume at dawn.
dialogue.afterScarcity: Primers are ink and patience. Both can be stretched.
dialogue.afterGrowth: A new stool filled. I chalked the roll myself.
dialogue.afterMission: The primers stayed open while you were on the road.
dialogue.afterLevel: New stools. Letters first, ledgers second, loyalty always.
